justification: Registers a genuinely new, sizeable data-quality finding (31 chapters flagged suspect, 29 of them new today) as a tracked ledger row with a real query-backed check, rather than leaving it in conversation only. Standard tier because it adds a new probe to scripts/dq_probe_live.py, not just prose.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: an active, needs_extraction chapter carries a suspect-alert key with nobody having reviewed it -- exits 1 with count 31 right now, by design (this is an open row, not declared fixed).
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Ran the probe before and after writing it: 31 both times, matching the live query I ran independently via dq_db.py first. dq_check.py PASSED (0 red, no declared-vs-actual mismatch) because this row is honestly declared 'open', matching its failing probe -- the exact ratchet this session's DQ-79/DQ-69 fixes exist to enforce is satisfied here from the start, not retrofitted.

pre_impl.existing_data: dcp_chapter_registry -- read-only throughout. Queried live via dq_db.py before writing anything: per-council breakdown (woollahra 22, ku_ring_gai 7, city_of_sydney 1, hornsby 1 = 31 total), confirmed the woollahra+ku_ring_gai 29 share one timestamp (2026-09-01 03:31:26 UTC) distinct from the city_of_sydney+hornsby 2's timestamp (2026-08-15), and confirmed is_active=True on every one of the 31 before claiming 'no served-data impact'.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Initially treated this as a single undifferentiated 'today's fire' before querying live -- the query revealed it is two unrelated populations (a 29-chapter spike and a 2-chapter standing item three weeks old), and that despite the spike's size, is_active=True on every row means the review queue already contained it. Also checked and ruled benign in the same pass: Canterbury-Bankstown's 53 'removed from hub' alert (68 active chapters, 0 flagged) and Waverley's HTTP 403 hub-scrape failure (a month-old gap, not new).
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: New row (DQ-89); does not touch or restate DQ-78, which covers a different council's map-label-scramble defect from a different extraction failure mode.

functions.name: PROBES['DQ-89'] (registered in scripts/dq_probe_live.py, dispatched by main())
functions.input: no CLI args beyond --id DQ-89; reads dcp_chapter_registry via the shared read-only dq_db session
functions.output: prints count + query + explanation to stdout, exits 1 if count > 0 else 0 -- unmodified dispatch shape shared with every other PROBES entry
functions.if_none: last_suspect_alert_key IS NOT NULL is the explicit null guard in the WHERE clause -- a chapter never flagged is correctly excluded, not miscounted as suspect

values.nullable: no, boolean not-null per schema (same table DQ-89's sibling probes already read)
values.guard_at: WHERE is_active AND needs_extraction, no null-handling needed

values.read_at: verified manually, not by this probe -- the probe deliberately does NOT filter on it beyond requiring TRUE, since a chapter that went inactive while flagged would be a different (and less urgent) situation than one still being served

queries.purpose: count the active suspect-flagged chapters and confirm served content is unaffected before writing the tracker row or the probe
queries.file_line: ad-hoc read-only queries via scripts/dq_db.py, then codified as the DQ-89 probe
queries.where_clause: dcp_chapter_registry WHERE is_active AND needs_extraction AND last_suspect_alert_key IS NOT NULL, grouped by council for the breakdown, filtered by council for the Canterbury-Bankstown/Waverley checks
queries.if_zero: would mean the spike had already cleared itself -- not the case, 31 confirmed live moments before writing this report
queries.if_wrong: cross-checked against the ops Telegram alert log's own council names and marker text (preflight_two_column, schema_fail, count_drop) -- exact match

break_it.scenario: DQ-89's count is read as 'served data is wrong for 31 chapters'.
break_it.what_happens: Someone escalates this as a live customer-facing defect when it is a queue holding correctly.
break_it.how: Both the tracker row and the probe note state explicitly and prominently that is_active=True on every counted row, so no served content is currently wrong -- this is a backlog-size check, not a correctness check.
break_it.repro: dcp_chapter_registry WHERE is_active AND needs_extraction AND last_suspect_alert_key IS NOT NULL AND NOT is_active returns 0

break_it.scenario: Someone 'fixes' DQ-89 by bulk-clearing needs_extraction on all 31 without reading any of them.
break_it.what_happens: A chapter with a real control interleaved with garbage text (DQ-78's own documented failure shape) gets committed as-is, hiding a real control -- the liability direction this project explicitly refuses.
break_it.how: The tracker row and dq_checks.json note both state this cannot be closed by a script and needs per-chapter human review, citing DQ-78 by name as the precedent for why.
break_it.repro: n/a -- a documentation safeguard, not a technical one; enforced by not shipping any clearing script here

break_it.scenario: The new probe conflates the 29-chapter spike with the pre-existing 2-chapter item, making it look like one homogeneous defect with one cause.
break_it.what_happens: Investigation time gets wasted looking for one root cause that explains both populations, when they are unrelated (three weeks apart, different councils).
break_it.how: The probe's own note explicitly separates the two by timestamp and names both council pairs distinctly.
break_it.repro: grep DQ-89 in dq_probe_live.py or DATA_QUALITY_TRACKER.md -- both state the split

break_it.scenario: The probe's count silently under- or over-counts because last_suspect_alert_key gets set/cleared by a path this query does not anticipate (e.g. a future extractor version stamps the key without also setting needs_extraction, or clears needs_extraction without clearing the key).
break_it.what_happens: DQ-89 would report a count that no longer means 'flagged AND unactioned', desynchronising the ledger from the actual review queue state.
break_it.how: Verified live, independently of the probe, that the three fields move together for all 31 current rows: every row with last_suspect_alert_key set also has needs_extraction=True and is_active=True, and the per-council breakdown from that independent query (woollahra 22, ku_ring_gai 7, city_of_sydney 1, hornsby 1) matches the probe's own count exactly.
break_it.repro: SELECT count(*) FROM dcp_chapter_registry WHERE last_suspect_alert_key IS NOT NULL AND NOT (is_active AND needs_extraction) -- returns 0 today, meaning the three fields are currently consistent; this query is worth re-running if the count ever looks surprising

post_merge.manual_verify: The actual investigation (opening Woollahra's migrated PDFs to determine whether this is a genuine new two-column typeset or a scraper artifact) is explicitly NOT done here -- tracked as open work in DQ-89, not resolved by it.
